name: recipe-layout
title: Recipe layout
description: A recipe page that cooks well: times and servings up front, ingredients that rescale, large-numeral steps with timers and a nutrition panel.
docs: Pass title, intro, times (prep, cook and total in minutes; the total is worked out when left out), servings (the number the quantities are written for), ingredients (quantity, unit, name, note, with unitPlural and plural for words that change, and group for a heading such as For the sauce), steps (text, an optional image and an optional timer in minutes), nutrition per serving, tips and onServingsChange. The stepper rescales every quantity the way a cook writes it: halves, thirds and quarters as fractions (1½ tbsp), grams and millilitres to the nearest 5 once they are big and as kilograms and litres past a thousand, 3 tsp as 1 tbsp, and a line without a quantity never scales. Set whole on an ingredient such as eggs to keep it a whole number. The new count is announced, and an amount that changes lights up for a moment. Steps are an ordered list with large numerals; a timer counts down in place against the clock, can be paused and reset, and is announced when it starts and ends; Start gives way to Pause and Reset brings Start back, with focus handed on so the keyboard keeps its place. Where the browser has the Wake Lock API a Keep screen awake switch appears; set keepAwake to false to remove it. The ingredients stay in view beside the steps from 1024px and come first on a phone. For search engines, structuredData writes schema.org Recipe data into the page from the same props (pass true, or an object with image, author, cuisine, category, datePublished and keywords); recipeJsonLd() in recipe-layout/schema gives you the same object to place yourself, written for the servings the recipe is written for. Pass labels and locale for another language.
